# Independent audit: binary root tree and actual full-star affinity



Audited sources:

- candidate 4c13e7d95b295d25
- candidate 9384183373b50261
- supporting computation verify_binary_root_coefficients_and_depth_obstruction.py

The standard-library verifier was rerun successfully. This audit also checks the mathematical arguments independently of the verifier.

## 1. Coefficients, binary digits, and the exact finite certificate

The coefficient recursion preserves the coordinate sum one and gives exactly the asserted parity. If a legal parent step is defined, it preserves the set of positive coordinates, including when the distinguished odd coordinate is negative. A path ending at a standard basis vector therefore has one positive coordinate.

Writing that vector as

\[
k=e_j+\sum_{i\ne j}m_i(e_j-e_i)
\]

is unique. At each step, no odd negative coefficient gives distinguished coordinate \(j\); exactly one odd negative coefficient gives that distinguished coordinate instead. Two or more odd negative coefficients are forbidden. The parent replaces every \(m_i\) by \(\lfloor m_i/2\rfloor\). Hence legality through termination is equivalent to pairwise disjoint binary supports. The converse and the zero-digit terminal case both hold.

The four-root construction has generation sizes \(1,3,9,27\), plus three external roots. The least significant digit gives the asserted parent inside the preceding generation. All radii are one, so root maximality and every positive power-weight requirement hold. The norm tie rule is correctly stated in coefficient space: the designated root is its color's unique point of squared norm one. The source explicitly retains the separate issue of a tie rule in projected actual base coordinates.

All ten table rows were checked using the exact closed inequalities, including boundary points. Their five-group counts are, in table order:

    (1,0,0,0,0), (3,1,0,0,0), (2,0,1,1,1),
    (0,0,0,1,3), (1,0,0,2,4), (0,0,0,0,1),
    (0,0,0,0,2), (0,0,0,0,3), (0,0,0,0,4),
    (0,0,0,0,7).

Permuting the same coordinates in the node and normal preserves the count, and the ten orbits exhaust the 43-point set. Thus every candidate has an actual containing closed cap of mass at most seven, and \(7<43/4\). This is a valid upper certificate; it does not require seven to be the exact maximum depth.

Under the specified square projection, the missing integer point \((-2,-2)\) has the exact convex representation

\[
(-2,-2)=\tfrac37(0,0)+\tfrac27(-7,0)+\tfrac27(0,-7).
\]

It is absent from the entire projected set. Consequently that projection cannot be the complete positive-fiber support of an actual convex family. No actual convex-family or OC counterexample follows from the coefficient certificate.

## 2. Full-star geometry and supporting majorants

The terminating forest puts every base in the affine span of the roots. The reflected partners at the designated star root form a centrally symmetric spanning set inside the base hull, so that root lies in its relative interior. The \(m=0\) case is correctly separated.

Passing to the convex hull of the positive integer fibers preserves all those fibers exactly. It gives positive full-dimensional continuous fibers at every real base in their convex hull. Both the volume-root function and each fixed-direction support function are finite concave functions there. Their supporting affine majorants at the relative-interior star root therefore exist.

For each reflected pair, the exact set midpoint identity makes the sum of the two majorant gaps zero. Since both gaps are nonnegative, both vanish. Radius saturation alone would not prove centroid affinity. The source correctly repeats saturation for actual support functions; subtracting the affine radius contribution and using the coordinate directions gives a single affine map for all root centroids. The terminating recursion propagates both affine identities to every fiber.

As an independent boundary check, finite sampled concavity itself also permits an affine majorant tight at any sampled base. Indeed, infeasibility of

\[
b\cdot(z-p)\ge r_z-r_p\quad(z\in P)
\]

would, by the finite linear alternative, give nonnegative coefficients with zero base displacement and positive radius displacement. Normalizing them would contradict the anchored concavity inequality at \(p\). The saved proof does not need this stronger boundary observation because its full-star hypotheses already give relative interior.

## 3. Weighted depth and precise realization scope

The positive-fiber base set is lattice-convex by positive-volume Minkowski interpolation. The finite weighted Doignon argument is valid in the saturated relative lattice of rank \(m\): any \(2^m\) atom subsets of weight greater than \((1-2^{-m})T\) share a positive-weight atom. The resulting integer intersection point lies in the actual base set. Complementary atoms are strictly outside a proposed smaller closed cap, so the closed-boundary contradiction has the correct direction. Rank zero is handled directly.

The affine centroid graph therefore has weighted depth at least \(T/2^m\). Ordinary Grünbaum in each counted full-dimensional fiber gives the asserted restricted-class mixed bound \(\Gamma_dT/2^m\), including vertical ambient cuts.

The original final-section phrase about an “injective affine realization” was potentially ambiguous: a map can be injective on finitely many nodes while lowering affine rank. The author corrected it to an affine embedding of the entire three-dimensional coefficient affine span and explicitly retained this finite-set distinction. The fixed 43-node, rank-two lattice-convex realization with the same small cap budgets is separately excluded by weighted Doignon. A completion adding positive weights must account for those weights; the audit does not transport the old seven-point cap counts to a completed family.

These are rigorous statements about the abstract coefficient model and the expressly restricted actual full-star class. They make no general zero-slack-forest or OC conclusion.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
